nodes.label: Storage in cubic metres,\narea in hectares
nodes.detail: `vol_sb` and `vol_fbas` are taken as cubic metres and `Red areal` as hectares, the units DP02 asks PULS to hold for basin volume and reduced area; the layers do not state them. The critical depth also leaves out what a structure passes on to the plant during rain, so it understates the rain a structure takes before it spills.

nodes.label: The rival pathways are\nsmooth in rainfall
nodes.detail: Runoff, riverine particulate organic carbon, buoyancy, resuspension and bather density are taken to respond smoothly to rainfall, with no threshold at any structure's storage depth. A rival with a threshold of its own near those depths would mimic the kink.

nodes.label: The far tail of the critical\ndepths is a unit error
nodes.detail: A critical depth far beyond any rain a structure could see - the largest runs to metres - is taken to come from storage or area recorded in the wrong unit, and the tail above the `p95` is set aside. No record says which structures are wrong.

nodes.label: Int means international
nodes.detail: The prefix Int in the layer's name Int vidå-kruså is read as international: the catchment with its part across the border, beside Vidå-kruså, its Danish part. The layer does not spell the prefix out.

nodes.label: A printed figure is rounded\nat its last non-zero digit
nodes.detail: SR353 prints its totals with trailing zeros after the digits that vary; each is taken as rounded to the nearest unit of its last non-zero digit, so the true value lies within half that unit. If the report rounded more coarsely, the bound on the page is too narrow.

nodes.label: Visits may avoid storms
nodes.detail: Bathing-water samples follow a programme set in advance, and a visit in a storm may be put off; nothing held records whether visits avoid storms. If they do, samples under-represent the exposure.
